chapter.title: Recap and Related APIs
chapter.description: A short tour of the remaining rendering escape hatches.

blocks.text: Forces React to apply a state update synchronously instead of batching it. Useful when you must read the DOM immediately afterwards - and slow, because it gives up batching.
`flushSync` is a last resort. It forces an extra synchronous render and defeats concurrent rendering. Check whether a layout effect or a callback ref does the job first.
Covered in the beginner track, but worth repeating here: changing a `key` is the cleanest way to force a subtree to rebuild with fresh state, and it beats a pile of reset effects.

items: Portals move DOM position without moving React position - context, events and boundaries all still work.
A modal needs focus management, Escape handling and scroll locking beyond the portal itself.
Strict Mode doubles work in development to reveal impure renders and missing cleanup.
`useInsertionEffect` is for style injection; `flushSync` is a rarely justified synchronous escape hatch.

previous.title: Strict Mode
previous.description: What the double invocations are checking, and why not to switch it off.

blocks.text: `StrictMode` is a development-only wrapper that surfaces unsafe patterns by doing things twice. It renders nothing itself and has no effect in production.

items: Calls component functions, initialisers, updaters and reducers **twice**, to expose impure logic.
Mounts, cleans up and remounts every component, to expose missing effect cleanup.
Warns about deprecated APIs and legacy string refs.

blocks.text: The doubling is the symptom, not the disease. A component that changes external state during render is already unreliable - React may call it more than once for its own reasons, including transitions and re-entrant renders.
Disabling Strict Mode because effects run twice hides a real bug rather than fixing it. Any component that remounts in production - a route revisited, a list reordered - hits exactly the same path.
A rarely used sibling of `useEffect` that runs before any DOM mutations. It exists for CSS-in-JS libraries that need to inject style rules before layout is calculated.
Unless you are writing a styling library, you will not need `useInsertionEffect`. It cannot read layout and it cannot use refs - it exists purely for the style injection timing problem.

blocks.title: Decide whether a click was inside a container
blocks.instructions: Complete isInside so it returns true when the target is the container or a descendant of it.

tests.name: A descendant counts as inside
tests.code: var b = document.createElement('div'); var c = document.createElement('span'); b.appendChild(c); return isInside(b, c) === true;

tests.name: The container itself counts
tests.code: var b = document.createElement('div'); return isInside(b, b) === true;

tests.name: An unrelated node is outside
tests.code: var b = document.createElement('div'); var o = document.createElement('p'); return isInside(b, o) === false;
